# AP-BAG-001 Staff Baggage Handling and Escalation

## 1. Purpose and Scope  
This policy establishes procedures for the handling of checked baggage throughout the airport's baggage handling system. It outlines the responsibilities of staff involved in the movement and management of baggage from the check-in belts to the baggage make-up area and onto aircraft. The policy ensures the safe, efficient, and compliant handling of all baggage, including the proper identification, labeling, and documentation of items. It also defines the escalation process for baggage incidents and the handling of restricted items. This policy applies to all staff involved in baggage handling, including Baggage Handlers, Baggage Duty Supervisors, and Ramp Leads.

## 2. Roles and Responsibilities  
The Baggage Handler is responsible for the physical handling of baggage, including loading, unloading, and sorting. The Baggage Duty Supervisor oversees the work of Baggage Handlers and ensures compliance with all baggage handling procedures. The Ramp Lead is responsible for coordinating baggage handling activities and ensuring that all operations are conducted safely and efficiently. All staff must follow established procedures, maintain accurate records, and report any incidents or anomalies in accordance with this policy. Each role has specific duties that contribute to the overall safety and efficiency of the baggage handling process.

## 3. Handling Standards  
All baggage must be handled with care to prevent damage, loss, or misrouting. Baggage Handlers must ensure that all bags are properly tagged and labeled in accordance with applicable regulations. Heavy bags must be handled using appropriate equipment to prevent injury. Fragile items must be clearly marked and handled with extra care to avoid damage. All baggage must be moved in a manner that minimizes the risk of injury to staff and passengers. Baggage Handlers must also ensure that all bags are correctly assigned to the correct aircraft and that all documentation is complete and accurate. Proper handling is essential to maintaining the integrity of the baggage handling system.

## 4. Baggage Incident Escalation  
When a baggage handler finds a damaged, leaking, or unattended checked bag in the baggage make-up area, the handler must escalate the incident to the Baggage Duty Supervisor within 10 minutes of discovery and must report it under AP-INC-002. All baggage incidents, including those involving damaged, leaking, or unattended bags, must be documented and reported promptly. The Baggage Duty Supervisor is responsible for ensuring that all incidents are investigated and resolved in accordance with established procedures. Escalation ensures that incidents are addressed in a timely manner and that appropriate actions are taken to prevent recurrence. All staff must be trained to recognize and report incidents in accordance with this policy.

## 5. Restricted Items Found in Baggage  
If a restricted item is found in a bag during baggage handling, the bag must not be further processed until it is approved or removed under the restricted-items approval procedure in AP-SEC-003. Baggage Handlers must immediately isolate the bag and notify the Baggage Duty Supervisor upon discovery of a restricted item. The Baggage Duty Supervisor is responsible for initiating the restricted-items approval procedure and ensuring that the bag is either approved for transport or removed from the baggage handling system. All staff must be aware of the procedures for handling restricted items and must follow them strictly to ensure compliance with security and safety regulations.

## 6. Records and Review  
All baggage incidents must be recorded in the incident log for review and analysis. The incident log must include details such as the time, location, and nature of the incident, as well as the actions taken. The Baggage Duty Supervisor is responsible for maintaining the incident log and ensuring that it is updated regularly. The policy will be reviewed annually to ensure its continued relevance and effectiveness. All staff must be trained on the procedures outlined in this policy and must be aware of their responsibilities in maintaining accurate records and ensuring compliance with all baggage handling standards. Regular review and training help ensure that the baggage handling process remains safe, efficient, and compliant with all applicable regulations.
